description:
Assistants get Lithuanian law wrong in a repeatable way: statute text on the web carries no date, so an answer about "article 52 of the Labour Code" is confidently right for some year and wrong for the one you are in.

Every answer here is for one point in time. It carries the validity window of the consolidated edition the words came from, and a URL on the official register where the same words and the same dates can be checked. Ten tools cover reading an article on a date, comparing two dates, listing which provisions changed between them, checking whether a citation made in an old document still holds, and listing amendments that are adopted but not yet in force.

When the register cannot confirm a point - a gap in the edition timeline, an act outside the curated catalogue of about 581 base acts, data too stale to stand behind - it says so and gives the reason. It does not guess. A refusal is never billed.

Data is published by the Chancellery of the Seimas and the State Data Agency under CC BY 4.0; the attribution travels in every response. This is published legislation, not legal advice.

defaultPrompt: What notice period does the Lithuanian Labour Code require on dismissal today?
How long do I have to accept an inheritance under Lithuanian law?
Was the same Labour Code in force in Lithuania in 2016 as today?
